title: Microsoft Teams: Copilot automatically summarises new messages in a chat
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, automatic-summary description, licence assignment path and PowerShell command are supported. Minor corrections should cite the existing prompt-driven chat experience and acknowledge Microsoft's bundled Copilot licensing option.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans for Copilot to generate a summary of new chat messages automatically without the user asking.

claims.claim: The planned summary lets users catch up without reading every missed message.
claims.quote: Missed many messages? Copilot will automatically generate a summary of the new messages in a chat conversation, so you can catch up quickly without reading every message.

claims.claim: The roadmap description names no admin or user step to enable the enhancement.
claims.quote: Missed many messages? Copilot will automatically generate a summary of the new messages in a chat conversation, so you can catch up quickly without reading every message.

claims.quote: Copilot will automatically generate a summary of the new messages in a chat conversation

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this specific automatic chat-summary enhancement.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams enhanced Copilot chat summary automatic new messages 501201'; read returned release-note excerpts and the Teams AI overview. No passage described this enhancement.

claims.claim: Existing Copilot in Teams chats and channels helps users catch up on conversations and contribute intelligently.
claims.quote: Copilot in your users’ chats and channels helps them catch up on conversations quickly and help contribute intelligently.

claims.claim: The existing chat-summary experience is something the user asks Copilot for.
claims.quote: Summarize chats and channel conversations | Type a prompt or select a prompt from **More prompts** in Copilot compose box in a chat or channel and submit.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/activity-reports/microsoft-365-copilot-usage to sources to support the comparison with the existing prompt-driven chat-summary experience.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft states that Copilot prompts, files and responses never leave the organisation's Microsoft 365 service boundary.
claims.quote: All prompts, files, and responses using Microsoft Copilot, including the Microsoft Copilot Chat app and the Microsoft Copilot app, never leave your organization’s Microsoft 365 service boundary.

claims.claim: No source describes this enhancement reaching content outside the chat being summarised.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams enhanced Copilot chat summary automatic new messages 501201'; read the roadmap description, Teams AI overview and returned release-note excerpts. No enhancement-specific description extended its content scope beyond the chat.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described a new identity, connection or permission for this enhancement.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams enhanced Copilot automatic new chat messages summary licensing price meter Copilot Chat Basic permissions'; read the roadmap, Teams AI overview, Copilot overview and returned excerpts. No new enhancement-specific identity, connection or permission was described.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a summary and does not describe additional actions.
claims.quote: Missed many messages? Copilot will automatically generate a summary of the new messages in a chat conversation, so you can catch up quickly without reading every message.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: No tenant or per-user UI or API switch specifically for automatic Copilot chat summaries in Teams is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams enhanced Copilot automatic chat summary 501201 admin setting policy disable automatic summaries'; opened Teams AI overview, Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy, Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy and manage-copilot-chat. No switch specific to automatic chat summaries was documented.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy has no Copilot chat-summary parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams automatic chat summary enhanced Copilot new messages identity permissions settings Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy'; opened Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy and searched its full text for 'Copilot' and 'summar'; neither occurred.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy has no Copilot chat-summary parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams automatic chat summary enhanced Copilot new messages identity permissions settings Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy'; opened Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy. Its settings concern EnrollFace, EnrollVoice, PassiveVoiceEnrollment and SpeakerAttributionBYOD, not chat summaries.

claims.claim: The cited meeting-policy Copilot controls describe Teams meetings and events, rather than chat summaries.
claims.quote: To manage how users in your org use Copilot in Teams meetings and events, use the -Copilot parameter within the PowerShell CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The cited calling-policy Copilot controls describe Teams calls, rather than chat summaries.
claims.quote: Teams calling policies control Copilot in one-to-one and group calls. Teams meeting policies control Copilot in scheduled meetings and Meet now.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: User licences are managed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section

claims.claim: The printed Set-MgUserLicense command assigns the selected product SKU to a user, acting on the licence rather than an individual chat summary.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Managing user licence assignments requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.
